questions.q: In the real dynamic array contract from this lesson, what does `getAllNumbers()` return?
questions.explain: getAllNumbers is a view function that returns the complete numbers array, unlike getNumber which returns just one indexed entry.

questions.q: Why can't you simply delete one element out of the middle of a dynamic array and have it shrink automatically?
options: Solidity doesn't support that directly — you have to shift later elements down manually, then pop the last one
Arrays automatically shrink whenever you delete anything
It's actually trivial and requires no extra code
Solidity has a single built-in function that does this in one step
questions.explain: Removing from the middle genuinely requires a real workaround: a for loop to shift every later element down by one, followed by pop() to remove the now-duplicated last entry.

questions.q: What does `require(_index < numbers.length, "Invalid index")` actually do?
options: Reverts the transaction with the message "Invalid index" if the condition is false
Always allows the function to continue, regardless of the index
Only logs a warning without stopping execution
questions.explain: require is a real guard clause — if the condition fails, the entire transaction reverts immediately with the given error message.

questions.q: What real use cases did the instructor name for array patterns like these?
options: Token balances, voting choices, whitelists, and history of actions
Exclusively used for storing Ethereum prices
questions.explain: The instructor explicitly named token balances, voting choices, whitelists, and action history as real-world uses of these exact array patterns.

questions.q: In `uint[3] public data = [1, 2, 3];`, what does `data[1]` (as returned by getSecond) actually equal?
options: An error, since index 1 doesn't exist
questions.explain: Since array indexes start at 0, index 0 holds 1, index 1 holds 2, and index 2 holds 3 — so data[1] returns 2.
